segments: 4. my people--the Jews. This reading is better than that of GESENIUS: "O peoples ... nations," namely, the Gentiles. entries.title: Isaiah 51:14
segments: 14. captive exile--literally, one bowed down as a captive (

) [MAURER].  The scene is primarily Babylon, and the time near the close of the captivity. Secondarily, and antitypically, the mystical Babylon, the last enemy of Israel and the Church, in which they have long suffered, but from which they are to be gloriously delivered. 
 
    pit--such as were many of the ancient dungeons (compare

entries.title: Isaiah 51:15
segments: 15. divided ... sea--the Red Sea. The same Hebrew word as "make to rest" (

). Rather, "that terrify the sea," that is, restrain it by My rebuke, "when its waves roar" [GESENIUS]. The Hebrew favors MAURER, "that terrify the sea so that the waves roar." The sense favors GESENIUS (
), or English Version (
, which favors the special reference to the exodus from Egypt).

entries.title: Isaiah 51:16
segments: 16. Addressed to Israel, embodied in "the servant of Jehovah" (

), Messiah, its ideal and representative Head, through whom the elect remnant is to be restored. 
 
    put my words in thy mouth--true of Israel, the depository of true religion, but fully realized only in Israel's Head and antitype, Messiah (

entries.title: Isaiah 51:18
segments: 18. Following up the image in

, intoxicated and confused by the cup of God's anger, she has none to guide her in her helpless state; she has not yet awakened out of the sleep caused by that draught.  This cannot apply to the Babylonish captivity; for in it they had Ezekiel and Daniel, Ezra and Nehemiah, as "guides," and soon awoke out of that sleep; but it applies to the Jews now, and will be still more applicable in their coming oppression by Antichrist.

entries.title: Isaiah 51:19
segments:
19. two--classes of evils, for he enumerates four, namely, desolation and destruction to the land and state; famine and the sword to the people. 
 
    who shall be sorry for thee--so as to give thee effectual relief: as the parallel clause, "By whom shall I comfort thee?" shows (

entries.title: Isaiah 51:20
segments: 20. head of all ... streets-- (

). 
 
    wild bull--rather, "oryx" [JEROME], or gazelle [GESENIUS], or wild goat [BOCHART]; commonly in the East taken in a net, of a wide sweep, into which the beasts were hunted together. The streets of cities in the East often have gates, which are closed at night; a person wishing to escape would be stopped by them and caught, as a wild animal in a net.
